html:
The founding of the Empire of Trebizond on the southeast coast of the Black Sea in 1204, by Alexios and David Komnenos, grandsons of the Byzantine emperor Andronikos I. It became one of the longest lasting Byzantine successor states.

The brothers had been raised at the court of Georgia, and with Georgian troops sent by Queen Tamar, their relative, they took Trebizond in April 1204, just before the crusaders took Constantinople. David pushed west but lost ground to Nicaea, and the state settled into a narrow coastal strip with the Pontic mountains behind it.

Its rulers, the Grand Komnenoi, grew rich on trade from Tabriz and Persia to the Black Sea, and paid tribute to the Seljuks and the Mongols when they had to. They married their daughters to Turkish and Georgian princes and built churches such as the Hagia Sophia. Trebizond outlived Constantinople by eight years: Mehmed II took it in 1461, in the fall of Trebizond.
sum: The founding of the Empire of Trebizond on the southeast coast of the Black Sea in 1204, by Alexios and David Komnenos, grandsons of the Byzantine emperor Andronikos I. It became one of the longest lasting Byzantine successor states.
